predecessors.name: Kingdom of France (Bourbon Restoration and July Monarchy)
predecessors.text: the French monarchy overthrown by the February Revolution of 24 February 1848

successors.name: Second French Empire
successors.text: France, the same outline, under the Empire proclaimed on 2 December 1852

ledger.x: 24 February 1848: the February Revolution overthrows the monarchy and the Second Republic is proclaimed.
ledger.cpn: Kingdom of France (Bourbon Restoration and July Monarchy)

ledger.x: 25 April 1849: French troops land to crush the Roman Republic.
July 1849: a French garrison stays in Rome.
2 December 1852 (dossier boundary only): the Republic ends and the garrison does not leave; the occupation continues under the Second French Empire, whose dossier reopens it and ends it in 1870.
2 December 1852: the Second Empire is established.

wars.name: French intervention against the Roman Republic (1849)
wars.outcome: The French took Rome on 3 July 1849 and restored the pope's temporal power; a French garrison propped up the papal administration until 1870.

certainty.note: Metropolitan frontiers unchanged through the Republic; the page records no boundary change.
